correctness.rationale: The Heawood Fano incidence graph has 14 vertices, 21 edges, 28 girth-six cycles, rank H1(graph)=8. Unordered Abrams D2 complex has 91 zero-, 252 one-, 168 two-cells; its Euler characteristic is 7. Ko–Park triconnected nonplanar graph theorem supplies H1 integral Z^8 plus Z/2; connectedness and Euler characteristic then force H2=Z^14 (cellular H2 is free). Signed cellular Hopf trace and the graph-chain projection yield the characters. Independently reconstructed the 168 Fano collineations plus one polarity, enumerated all 336 graph automorphisms, and counted oriented cellular fixed-cell traces; result exactly [(order, exchanges?, count, trH1, trH2)]=(1,False,1,8,14),(2,False,21,0,-2),(2,True,28,-2,-2),(3,False,56,-1,-1),(4,False,42,0,2),(6,True,56,1,1),(7,False,48,1,0),(8,True,84,0,0). Averaging over all 336 and over the 168 preserving automorphisms gives zero positive-degree invariant ranks. The 28 six-cycles span graph H1, so the natural equivariant map H1(D2)->H1(graph) is an isomorphism. These exact finite combinatorial checks really exhaust this finite graph, while the prior integral H1 theorem supplies torsion.
residual_risks: Diagnostic finite computations alone cannot establish an infinite-dimensional or asymptotic assertion; unrestricted scope depends on reconstructed analytical argument.
